input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 (p0013) binds Customer to Vendor as its sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the whole term, with no product-category narrowing, no 12-month limit, and no automatic exit for missed service levels or delivery dates. That is full-term exclusive dealing without a performance-based exit — walk-away territory, and it fails every fallback element. Sections 2.1 (no minimum or purchase commitment) and 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges no exclusivity commitment) point the other way but do not override the express appointment in 2.2, so the internal conflict must be resolved in the operative clause. We target the preferred position by making the appointment non-exclusive and confirming no Customer exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation, which also cures the conflict with 2.1 and 12.3. No exclusivity running in Customer's favour is affected.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.

proposal.summary: Convert Section 2.2 from sole-and-exclusive provider to non-exclusive, with no Customer exclusivity obligation
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot appoint Vendor as our sole and exclusive provider, so we have made Section 2.2 non-exclusive and confirmed we carry no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation, consistent with Sections 2.1 and 12.3. If you need protection, we could discuss exclusivity limited to a defined product category for no more than 12 months, ending automatically on any missed service level or delivery date.

ops.oldText: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
ops.newText: Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services, and Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
